newsitem.title: LATVIA: Amoco denies warning Latvia on oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Amoco denies warning Latvia on oil deal.

text.p: U.S. oil company Amoco Corp denied on Wednesday that it has warned Latvia it will rip up an oil exploration deal if the Baltic state does not settle a maritime border row with neighbour Lithuania.

Latvian radio earlier reported that Amoco told Lithuanian parliament speaker Vytautas Landsbergis during a visit to Washington that it would unilaterally scrap the exploration deal if the dispute was not solved quickly.
"We are ready to keep waiting and we have already waited," Valdis Budrevics, Amoco vice president of overseas exploration in charge of the Baltic Sea region, told Reuters.
"We have not voiced any warning or come up with announcements," he added.

Amoco and Swedish state-owned Olje Prospektering (OPAB) signed a deal with Latvia to explore a small part of the Baltic Sea. But Latvia has not yet settled its sea border with Lithuania in the region and talks are currently deadlocked.
Latvia went ahead and ratified the agreement with Amoco, enraging the Lithuanians.
"The position of both Amoco and OPAB since late last year is that neither of us meddle in politics. This is an issue to be settled by two soveregin countries," he added.
"At the moment there is nothing else left for us but to wait and see," Budrevics added.
